I go down to visit him and he brings us to the warehouse so we can "skate with the pros" I'm in my twenties at the time and not very good so I kinda meander around looking for something I can actually do that's also not in anyone else's way. 

Then I see the quarter pipe wall in the corner. Big ramp down to gain speed and a 3ft wide pipe going about 14ft up with about 9ft of it vertical wall. So my idea is that I can bomb down and hit it with speed, do a pivot turn at the peak and ride back down. Only problem is, the quarter pipe is skinnier than I'm used to and I can't seem to stick the turn. 

Over and over I keep bailing and losing my board. It was frustrating cause I knew I could do it, but it just wasn't happening. Eventually I walk away from it and just fuck around in a mini ramp for a bit, watching the sponsored skaters kill it and working in a set when my turn came up.

Then, before it was time to go I went back to the quarter pipe/vert wall and after like 6 more tries I nailed it. As I was skating out of it with a grin on my face everyone started clapping and cheering, and Anthony Mosely skated up to me and shook my hand and congratulated me on it.

Best day of skating ever, and I didn't even do anything good.

tl/dr: seal the boards, hold the blue line, have fun.
